title: Shortest Path with Alternating Colors
summary: Given an integer n representing the number of nodes in a directed graph with nodes labeled from 0 to n-1, and two arrays redEdges and blueEdges indicating directed red and blue edges, return an array answer of length n.
statement: Given an integer n representing the number of nodes in a directed graph with nodes labeled from 0 to n-1, and two arrays redEdges and blueEdges indicating directed red and blue edges, return an array answer of length n. Each answer[x] represents the shortest path length from node 0 to node x with alternating edge colors, or -1 if no such path exists.
constraints: Paths start at node zero and consecutive edge colors must alternate.
Return shortest distance to every node or -1.
hints: BFS state must include both node and color of the last edge.
Seed node zero with both imaginary prior colors.
From each state traverse only the opposite-color adjacency list and visit each (node,color) once.
BFS levels give shortest alternating distances while the color state enforces legality.
editorial: BFS levels give shortest alternating distances while the color state enforces legality.

tests.explanation: Node one is one red edge away, but node two cannot use two red edges consecutively.
Alternating red then blue reaches distances zero,one,two.
